property_summary: After any call to Put, the contract's balance must equal the sum of all accumulated holder balances, which the reference always preserves via the overflow check; the buggy version violates this invariant when an overflow occurs in acc.balance += msg.value.

After a call to Put, the holder's balance is always at least the msg.value sent in that call, which the reference preserves via the overflow check, but the buggy version violates when overflow occurs in acc.balance += msg.value.

For every actor and amount, after Put is called, the holder's unlockTime is correctly set to the maximum of the passed _unlockTime and block.timestamp, which the reference always does; the buggy version violates this when the overflow check is absent and msg.value causes an overflow, leading to a revert that prevents the unlockTime update.

For every actor that calls Put with a positive msg.value, the caller's Acc balance in the reference contract must be strictly greater than the balance before the call, but the buggy version can leave it unchanged when overflow resets it.

After a successful call to Put, the contract's balance minus the sum of all holders' balances is exactly the initial contract balance, meaning no ether is lost or unaccounted for; the buggy version violates this invariant when an overflow in acc.balance += msg.value causes the holder's balance to wrap around, making the sum of balances inconsistent with the contract's actual ether holdings.

After any Put call, the unlock time stored in Acc[msg.sender] must equal the max of the given _unlockTime and block.timestamp; the buggy version always sets it to block.timestamp, violating this rule when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

After two successive Put calls by the same sender with different unlockTime parameters, the unlockTime stored in Acc[sender] reflects the second call's unlockTime in the reference, but the buggy version incorrectly ignores it and uses block.timestamp.

For any single Put call, if the supplied _unlockTime is greater than the current block.timestamp, the resulting Acc[caller].unlockTime must equal _unlockTime; the buggy version always sets it to block.timestamp, violating this when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

For any Put call, the resulting Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime must be greater than or equal to the given _unlockTime parameter; the mutant sets it to block.timestamp, violating the rule when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.
After a Put call, the unlockTime must be at least the supplied _unlockTime; the buggy version ignores _unlockTime and uses block.timestamp, violating this when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.
After any Put call, the sender's Acc balance should equal the sum of their balance before the call plus the msg.value sent; the buggy early-return makes the balance unchanged.
After a successful Put call, the sender's account unlockTime must be at least block.timestamp; the buggy early-return leaves unlockTime at its default 0, violating this for any non-zero call.

After a call to Put, the timestamp of the last log message in the Log file's History must be equal to the block timestamp of the Put call; the buggy no-op does not add a message, so the last log timestamp remains unchanged.
After a successful Put call, the sender's Acc balance must be strictly greater than zero; the buggy early-return leaves the balance at 0.

After a successful call to Put(msg.value > 0), the length of the Log History array must increase by exactly 1; the buggy early-return prevents any log message from being added, leaving the History length unchanged.

For any call to Put, the caller's recorded balance in Acc[msg.sender].balance must equal the total ether previously sent by that caller to Put; the bug breaks this by incrementing by a fixed 100 ether instead of msg.value.

For any call to Put by any caller, the recorded balance in Acc[msg.sender].balance must be at least the total ether sent by that caller to Put; the bug violates this because it adds a fixed 100 ether, which can be less than msg.value when msg.value > 100 ether.

For any call to Put with msg.value, the contract's ETH balance must increase by at least msg.value; the bug increments the caller's recorded balance by a fixed 100 ether instead of msg.value, so when msg.value > 100 ether, the contract holds less ETH than the sum of all recorded balances.

After any sequence of calls to Put by the same sender, the contract's ETH balance must be at least the sender's recorded Acc balance; the bug adds 100 ether instead of msg.value, so when a sender calls Put with msg.value < 100 ether, the recorded balance exceeds the sender's total contribution and therefore the contract's actual ETH balance.

For any call to Put, the increase in the contract's ETH balance must equal msg.value; the bug adds a fixed 100 ether to the caller's recorded balance regardless of msg.value, causing the contract's balance change to diverge from the sum of recorded balance changes.
Collect only succeeds when block.timestamp is greater than the sender's unlockTime.

Collect returns without revert if and only if block.timestamp is strictly greater than the _unlockTime passed to Put.

When block.timestamp is not greater than the holder's unlockTime, a non-empty Collect call will revert in the reference but succeed in the mutant, changing the contract's ETH balance.
After any call to Collect, the caller's unlocked balance (balance when block.timestamp > unlockTime) can never decrease before unlockTime in the reference, but the mutant allows it to decrease.

For any address that has a balance and an unlockTime, if a call to Collect succeeds before the unlockTime, then the unlockTime must be in the future relative to the caller's stored unlockTime; the reference always reverts for amounts <= balance before unlockTime, while the mutant succeeds, violating the invariant that Collect never succeeds before unlockTime.

For any caller, after a Collect call before their unlockTime, the reference never decreases the caller's balance (because it reverts or no-ops), while the mutant decreases it, violating the invariant that balance remains unchanged before unlockTime.
